layout_dets.text: On the Mechanism for Improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Passivation by Additions of Tungsten

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to Austenitic Stainless Steels*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N. BUI, * A. IRHZO, * F. DABOSI, * and Y. LIMOUZIN-MAIRE**

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In order to elucidate the role of W in improving the passivity of austenitic stainiess steels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anodic polarization curves and X-ray photoelectron spectra have been obtained for pure W

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and W-containing steels passivated in 1 N HCl, 0.1 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and in Cl--containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Similar experiments were also performed on Cr-Ni steels passivated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results showed that pure tungsten by itself does not develop a protective layer and that alloy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing tungsten inhibits pitting corrosion, as do tungstate ions dissolved in neutral chloride solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. In the passive layer, tungstate ions were found to be adsorbed without reduction, and in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the case of alloying tungsten, this element is present under the + VI oxidation state. Alloying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tungsten is thought to pass directly from the metal into the passive film, by interaction with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: water and formation of insoluble

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which enhances the stability of oxide layers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is weil known that additions of Mo to austenitic stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels improve their passivity, particularly their resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting in chloride solutions.i,2,12 It has aiso been shown that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying W increases the corrosion resistance of austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20Cr-25Ni steels in acid chloride solutions.3,4 The primary pur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pose of W additions to stainiess steels was to improve their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanical resistance to abrasion corrosion in the wet proc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ess of phosphoric acid production.³ While many attempts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were made to clarify the role of molybdenum additions by XPS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and AES surface analysis,2,5-9 the mechanism for improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivation by alloying tungsten has not been investigated, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: far as we know in our survey of literature. The present study is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an attempt to elucidate the role of W in the improvement of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film stability. Previously, experimental 16Cr-14Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels with varying amounts of W, up to 12 Wt%,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were prepared, and polarization measurements in acid chlo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ride and fluoride solutions were performed.11 The results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showed that in all cases the additions of tungsten to stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels reduce the anodic dissolution rate and enhance their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivation. As W and Mo are in the same column of the peri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: odic tabie and have similar chemical properties, the question

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is whether alloyed W will have the same role as Mo in stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel. If so, the following propositions, as stated in Reference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2), are possible in interpreting the effect of W on passivity: (1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickening of the passive films of the steels, (2) forming a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heteropoly-acid film which is less hydrolyzed and more readily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polymerized, (3) impeding the adsorption of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: onto the sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: face of the steel by increasing the oxygen affinity of the steel,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (4) forming an amorphous oxide film with a glassy struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the present investigation, it is proposed to answer the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following questions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Does W by itself form a protective film, without interac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion with other elements such as Cr, Ni, Fe?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Does dissolution of alloyed W result in the formation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions which will inhibit the pitting process in neutral

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride solution? How effective is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as pitting inhibitor?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For these purposes, polarization measurements of pure W

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were carried out in 1 N HCl and in 40 Wt%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1000 ppm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: .Then similar experiments were performed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compare the effect of W either as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions dissolved in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neutral chloride solution or as alloying element in the steels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ESCA measurements were subsequently conducted on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passive films formed on the surface of W-containing Cr-Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels and on Cr-Ni steels passivated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental results were used to discuss the role of W on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: basis of the above questions.

layout_dets.text: Experimental Procedures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The five experimental austenitic 16Cr-14Ni alloys contain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing 0 to 12 Wt% were prepared in a vacuum furnace. Speci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mens were cut from rolled sheet of these alloys, having a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness of 5 mm and a diameter of 12 mm. Their chemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions are given in Table 1. Solution treatment was per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed by heating in nitrogen at 1150 C for 30 minutes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: followed by water quenching. For electrochemical measure-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment, the surfaces studied were mechanically polished with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emery paper under water up to grade 1000, then were degreas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ed in absolute ethyl alcohol, washed in deionized water, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dried by warm air blowing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Polarization curves were obtained potentiodynamically at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a scan rate of 20 mV/min, using a Tacussel electrochemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set composed of a potentiostat, a current recorder, and a high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impedance electronic millivoltmeter.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The valency of alloyed W in the passive film formed on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels in chloride solutions was investigated by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: means of ESCA spectroscopy, a surface sensitive technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which gives photoelectron spectra of elements in different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: valence states, in particular in metallic and oxide forms. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrument was a Vacuum Generators ESCA 4. The samples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were irradiated with Al Kα radiation, with a mean energy of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1486.6 eV. Photoelectron spectra of 4 d3/2 and 4 d5/2 levels of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: W were recorded. The binding energies at the peaks observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the photoelectron spectra were corrected using the value of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the energy of carbon 1s level (285 eV) observed in the back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground spectrum.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results and Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical Behavior of Pure W

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Anodic polarization curve of pure W in 1 N HCl and in 40

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wt%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing 1000 ppm Cl-, at 60 C, are shown in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1. It can be seen that corrosion potential of W is – 0.10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: V vs SCE, a value much higher than that of 16Cr-14Ni (- 0.37

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: V), in 1 N HCl. Pure Mo, on the other hand, also has a high cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion potential, – 0.03 V in 1 N HCl at 25 C, as measured by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other authors.² The main feature, however, is that W, as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, dissolves at a high rate in the passive region of the W con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining 16Cr-14Ni steels or 20Cr-25Ni-5Mo steels. In other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: words, Mo and W alloying elements increase the pitting re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance of stainless steels in the potential region where they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are highly active in pure form. This suggests that W does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protect by making a stable oxide layer, but only by interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with other oxides. Sugimoto and Sawada² have shown that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combination of Mo and Ni, as well as those of Mo and Fe, do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not result in an increase in pitting resistance. It is thought that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: W improves the pitting inhibition, just like Mo, when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of Cr is above an adequate level in the alloy. It has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIGURE 1 — Anodic behavior of pure tungsten.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been shown previously that alloyed W improves the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of 20Cr-25Ni-4Mo steels.³ This means that W might

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have an additive action with Mo and might have the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism as Mo in forming a passive oxide layer with chro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mium.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inhibitive Properties of Tungstate lons

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the hypothesis that the dissolution of alloyed W results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the formation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions, polarization studies were car-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ried out with 16Cr-14Ni steel in 0.1 M NaCl containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at various concentrations, in order to evaluate the inhibitive ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in solution. Figure 2 shows the anodic polariza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion curves obtained in 0.1 M NaCl containing 0 to 0.025 to 0.1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at 60 C.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It can be seen that an increase in tungstate concentration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from 0 to 0.1 M results in an elevation of corrosion potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from - 360 to – 230 mV (vs SCE) and at the same time a great

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decrease in passive current density.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CORROSION—NACE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIGURE 2 — Anodic behavior of 16Cr-14Ni steels in 0.1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: M NaCl with various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIGURE 3 — Anodic polarization curves of W-containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels in 0.1 M NaCl (curve numbering refers to Table 1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The improvement of the passivity characteristics is fur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ther illustrated by the shifts of breakdown potentials to higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values: 80, 150, and 220 mV vs SCE, respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For comparison, the effect of alloyed W was studied by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determining the electrochemical behavior of W-containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels in 0.1 M NaCl without tungstate. In Figure 3, it is shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that corrosion potential increases and passive current density

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases with increasing W content in the steels, but the ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fect is less pronounced than that produced by tungstate in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution. However, the effect of alloyed W in increasing the pit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting potentials is greater.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These potential values are now 80, 210, and 300 mV vs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SCE, respectively, for 0, 2, and 4% W in 16Cr-14Ni steels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These results point out that the effect of alloying W is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: somewhat similar to adding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 0.1 M NaCl solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There is, however, a little difference; while tungstate in solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion has the effect of shifting the passivity range (i.e., the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential difference between pitting potential and corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential) in the noble direction of potential without changing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it, alloying W has a greater tendency to extend this passivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The action of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in solution may be explained by an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorption process which has already occurred at the corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion potential. According to Rosenfeld,1² the oxide film formed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through a natural process on the metal surface changes its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties when insignificant amounts of inhibitor are ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sorbed. This modification is of structural and electrophysical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature rather than a variation of thickness or continuity of pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tective films. This proposed mechanism may be extended to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the role of alloyed W. This element could be present in the ox-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ide film which is instantaneously formed in air and could make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a significant contribution to modify the passive properties of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film, by accepting oxide electrons and strengthening the oxide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film crystal lattice.12 At the corrosion potential, where the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissolution rate of W is very low, it is unlikely that alloyed W

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in solution which later on will act as inhibitor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by adsorption. It has been shown that during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorp-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, chromium is reduced from (+ VI to the, + IIl valency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state12) and that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may be reduced to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ESCA studies were undertaken to determine what W oxidation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: states were present in the oxide film and whether there is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduction of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during adsorption.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ESCA Study of the Passive Film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Prior to the examination, the passive film was developed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the surface by maintaining the sample for 15 minutes at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: – 50 mV/SCE, a potential situated in the middle of the passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range, as can be seen in Figure 2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For 16Cr-14Ni steel passivated in 0.1 M NaCi + 0.05 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution, ESCA spectrum of the surface layer (Figure 4)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows two peaks corresponding to tungsten, situated at 247.6

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 260.3 eV.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Pure tungsten does not develop a protective layer but,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in alloy form, improves the pitting resistance of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels in acid or neutral chloride solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. The tungstate ion dissolved in neutral chloride solution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inhibits pitting corrosion of 16Cr-14Ni steel, as does alloying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tungsten.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. ESCA study of the passive film indicates that tung-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state was adsorbed without modification of oxidation state

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and that alloying tungsten is also present in the passive layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the + VI state.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. In acid chloride solutions, W probably passes directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the metal into the passive film, by interaction with water

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and formation of insoluble

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rather than through a dissolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion then adsorption process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. In neutral chloride solution, the beneficial effect of W

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is interpreted by the interaction of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with other oxides,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in enhanced stability and enhanced bonding of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxide layers to the base metal.

layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A solvent composed of 8% EDTA, 2% citric acid, and 0.5% hydrazine, used at pH 6, and which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was developed for the chemical cleaning of nuclear steam generators, was studied at 95 C for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its agressiveness against carbon steel. Corrosion protection is improved by adding sulfur-free

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: organic inhibitors to the pure solvent. In spite of this, when simulating the presence of corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion products by adding magnetite, the effect of such inhibitors, as well as the corrosivity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pure solvent, may be radically affected. Furthermore, different supplies of magnetite,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether they are added to the pure or the inhibited solvent, may have different solubilities and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can drastically affect the corrosion rates. This might be explained in terms of the hydrazine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evolution and/or the effective hydrazine content in solution during the test. It is found, never-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theless, that synergistic effects between surfactants and inhibitors could inhibit carbon steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion, regardless of the supply of magnetite used. A mixture of benzotriazole, Triton X-100,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Chevron NI-W has been found useful as an inhibitor to chemical cleaning solvents of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type considered.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the last few years, a considerable amount of research on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical cleaning of nuclear steam generators has been per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed in many laboratories. Among other aspects studied,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the corrosion mechanisms involved in the use of the cleaning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solvents,1-5 and the development of process applications6-12

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been extensively explored. The first successful chemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cleaning of an operational pressurized-water reactor type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boiler was carried out at the end of 1979,13 and the technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is now a recognized means of decelerating or stopping various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion phenomena detrimental to many units.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Applied to dissolve the corrosion products transported to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or formed in a steam generator, solvents based on chelating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agents are aggressive toward unailoyed steels and corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inhibitors are therefore added to protect them. The best in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hibitors used so far for that purpose are often based on sulfur

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compounds, but the possibility that these might be detrimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tal to Inconel 600, which proves susceptible to intergranular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stress corrosion cracking in the presence of some sulfur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing species,14,15 has created the need to look at new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: substitutes. This aspect of materials protection through the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition of organic corrosion inhibitors to chemical cleaning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solvents based on chelating agents is still grossly under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: developed. Hausler16 studied the corrosion mechanism on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel of a solvent based on 10% EDTA and 1% hydrazine.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: From a parametric study, he interpreted the general inhibition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism observed with and without magnetite and a com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mercial inhibitor, and found that the corrosion rates in such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
